forecast-period.text: A high pressure system centred in the Bight will slowly move over southeastern Australia this week while maintaining a ridge over SA. A trough will pass by the coast mid week before a stronger cold front begins to move into the Bight this weekend.
For latest warnings go to www.bom.gov.au, subscribe to RSS feeds, call 1300 659 210* or listen for warnings on relevant TV and radio broadcasts.
* Calls to 1300 numbers cost around 27.5c incl. GST, higher from mobiles or public phones.

Patchy morning fog and about parts of the agricultural areas and southern parts of the pastoral districts. Mostly dry. Maximum temperatures near average in the west, grading to below average in the east. Light winds in the south tending northeast to southeasterly in the north.
Mostly dry. Southwest to southeasterly winds, fresh at times about the southeast coast.

Morning frost and possible fog on and east of the ranges. Mostly dry, chance of an isolated shower in the far west in the morning. Maximum temperatures near average, tending below average in the southeast. Light winds in the east, tending northwest to northeasterly elsewhere. Winds turning southeasterly in the west during the day.
Morning frost and possible fog on and east of the ranges. Mostly dry. Maximum temperatures near to above average. East to northeasterly winds.

text.p: Morning frost on and east of the ranges. Isolated showers developing in the far west during the morning, reaching the eastern districts during the evening. The chance of a thunderstorm in the far west. Maximum temperatures near to above average. Northeast to northwesterly winds, fresh at times over central districts during the day.
Cumulative rainfall totals to the end of Thursday: Less than 2 mm about the agricultural areas, tending 2-5 mm about the far west.
